html:
SMTO-POL-0004 — SMTO needs you to confirm this risky action

GUID: c35b5e57-b0ad-437e-a33f-51b4af0135ee
Slug: unsafe-authorization-required
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Task wants to run an action that could delete data, change the system or interrupt a service. It's waiting for you to confirm this exact action; approving other actions doesn't cover it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the confirmation window (usually titled Unsafe action requires confirmation), read Target and Exact operation. They show exactly which computer and which command your confirmation would allow.
  2. Select the confirm button, usually Proceed (or Restart, Shut down and similar), to run it, or Cancel to stop it. SMTO runs this action only after you confirm this exact operation.
  3. Decide within about five minutes. If the window says the authorization expired, select Cancel and ask the Agent for the action again. Confirmations expire so an old one can't be used for a later action.
  4. To change when SMTO asks, an administrator can change Unsafe actions in Settings › Security. Ask means you confirm each risky action, and Disallow blocks them.

What success looks like

  • The confirmation window closes and the step runs in the Task's activity, or the Task stops if you selected Cancel.

If it still fails

  • If no confirmation window appears, reload the page. If it's still missing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The unsafe-action checkpoint (unsafe_action_policy = ask) intercepted a destructive or host-control invocation and requires a confirmation bound to the exact proposed operation and target before granting authority.

What this means

  • The unsafe-action checkpoint requires a decision bound to the exact proposed operation before granting its supported authority. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The unsafe-action checkpoint requires a decision bound to the exact proposed operation before granting its supported authority.

How to diagnose it

  • Review the pending operation, target and displayed risk against your intent; reject or revise it if any of those differ.

How to fix it

  • Confirm or cancel the exact pending operation through the unsafe-action dialog (POST /api/agent/native/<request_id>/unsafe-action with the current challenge_id). Change the unsafe_action_policy setting only if the policy itself should differ.
  • Review and approve the exact current operation through the existing approval flow if intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The current checkpoint records the user's deliberate decision for the unchanged operation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
